mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a granny flat and an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both provide independent living space, a granny flat traditionally features design elements tailored to aging relatives, whereas an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a broader zoning classification. ADUs include detached backyard cottages, basement apartments, and garage conversions built for various uses, including long-term rental or guest housing. Granny flats often prioritize accessibility features such as walk-in showers, zero-threshold entries, and wider doorways to support aging in place. When deciding between the two, consider whether your primary goal is long-term family care or general multi-use flexible living space.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a broad zoning term for any secondary residential unit, while a granny flat specifically emphasizes independent, accessible living space for family members.
